questions.question: Which term describes a sculpture meant to be viewed from all sides?
questions.correctAnswer: Sculpture in the round
questions.explanation: Sculpture in the round is freestanding and finished on every side, unlike relief sculpture which is attached to a background.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Walk all the way around me - I look good from every angle, and so does sculpture in the round!

questions.question: Carving is an example of which sculptural process?
questions.correctAnswer: Subtractive
questions.explanation: Carving removes material from a block, so it is subtractive. Modeling and assembling add material, so they are additive.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Carving is like erasing - you take away until the shape appears!

questions.question: Which material is most commonly associated with modeling, an additive process?
questions.correctAnswer: Clay
questions.explanation: Clay is soft and buildable, making it ideal for the additive process of modeling. Marble and granite are carved, and steel is welded or cast.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Squish it, stack it, shape it - clay loves to be added together!

questions.question: A sculpture that projects only slightly from a flat background is called
questions.correctAnswer: Low relief (bas-relief)
questions.explanation: Bas-relief (low relief) barely rises from its background, like images on coins. High relief projects dramatically outward.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bas-relief is shy - it only peeks out a little from the wall!

questions.question: In the 3-D printing workflow, slicer software is used to
questions.correctAnswer: Convert a 3-D model file into stacked layers and machine instructions
distractors: Photograph the finished print for a portfolio
Mix two resins into a new printing material
Sand and polish the surface of a finished print
questions.explanation: A modeling program produces geometry, not machine moves. The slicer cuts that geometry into horizontal layers, decides wall thickness and infill, and writes the toolpath file the printer actually follows.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The slicer is the translator - it turns your 3-D model into instructions the printer can follow!

questions.question: An armature is used in sculpture to
questions.correctAnswer: Support the structure of a modeled form
questions.explanation: An armature is an inner skeleton, usually wire or wood, that holds up soft modeled materials like clay.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Even sculptures need bones - the armature is the skeleton inside!

questions.question: Which of these describes an assemblage technique?
questions.correctAnswer: Joining found objects into a sculpture
distractors: Throwing a pot on a wheel
questions.explanation: Assemblage is an additive process that builds sculpture by combining found or manufactured objects.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: One dino's trash is another dino's sculpture - assemblage!

questions.question: Michelangelo's David was created using which process?
questions.correctAnswer: Carving marble
questions.explanation: Michelangelo subtractively carved the David from a single block of Carrara marble between 1501 and 1504.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Michelangelo freed David from the marble - he just removed everything that was not David!

questions.question: The term maquette refers to
questions.correctAnswer: A small preliminary model for a larger sculpture
questions.explanation: Artists build maquettes to test composition and solve structural problems before committing to full scale.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A maquette is a sculpture's baby photo - small now, huge later!

questions.question: Pinch, coil, and slab are methods of
questions.correctAnswer: Hand-building with clay
questions.explanation: These are the three fundamental hand-building techniques: pinching, coiling ropes of clay, and joining flat slabs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Pinch it, coil it, slab it - three ways to build without a wheel!

questions.question: Before its first firing, unfired clay is called
questions.correctAnswer: Greenware
questions.explanation: Greenware is dry but unfired clay. After the first (bisque) firing it becomes bisqueware.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Greenware is not green - it is just not baked yet!

questions.question: Clay that is firm but still damp enough to carve or attach handles is at what stage?
questions.correctAnswer: Leather-hard
questions.explanation: Leather-hard clay holds its shape but can still be carved, trimmed, and joined - the ideal working stage for refinement.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Leather-hard feels like a chocolate bar - firm but you can still carve it!

questions.question: What is the purpose of bisque firing?
questions.correctAnswer: To harden the clay so it can be glazed safely
distractors: To melt the glaze onto the surface
To add color to the clay
questions.explanation: The bisque (first) firing makes greenware durable enough to handle during glazing, though it remains porous enough to absorb glaze.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bisque firing is the clay's first bake - it gets tough enough for its glaze coat!

questions.question: Centering is the first step in which ceramic technique?
questions.correctAnswer: Wheel-throwing
questions.explanation: On the potter's wheel, the clay must be centered - spinning perfectly true - before it can be opened and pulled into a vessel.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Center first, or your pot will wobble like a dizzy dinosaur!

questions.question: Earthenware, stoneware, and porcelain differ mainly in
questions.correctAnswer: Firing temperature and vitrification
distractors: The tools used to shape them
questions.explanation: Earthenware fires lowest and stays porous; stoneware vitrifies at mid-range temperatures; porcelain fires highest to a glassy, translucent body.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Hotter kiln, tougher clay - earthenware, stoneware, porcelain climb the temperature ladder!

questions.question: In reduction firing, the kiln atmosphere
questions.correctAnswer: Is starved of oxygen, affecting glaze color
distractors: Is flooded with oxygen for brighter colors
Removes all glaze from the work
questions.explanation: Reduction limits oxygen so flames pull oxygen from the glazes themselves, producing distinctive effects like copper reds and celadons.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: No air for the flames? The glaze pays the price - and looks amazing!

questions.question: Glaze is applied to ceramics to
questions.correctAnswer: Create a glassy, often waterproof surface
questions.explanation: Glaze melts in the kiln into a glass coating that seals the surface and adds color and texture.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Glaze is the shiny raincoat that ceramics wear!

questions.question: What is a common cause of clay exploding in the kiln?
questions.correctAnswer: Trapped air or moisture in the clay
distractors: Firing at too low a temperature
questions.explanation: Air pockets or water turn to steam and expand violently at high heat, so clay must be wedged and fully dry before firing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bubbles in clay go BOOM in the kiln - wedge them out first!

questions.question: Raku firing is distinctive because
questions.correctAnswer: Hot pieces are removed from the kiln and placed in combustible materials
distractors: It fires at the highest cone temperatures
questions.explanation: In raku, glowing-hot work goes into sawdust or newspaper, creating smoky crackled surfaces through rapid cooling and reduction.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Raku is the daredevil firing - grab it hot and bury it in sawdust!

questions.question: Trimming a wheel-thrown pot is best done when the clay is
questions.correctAnswer: Leather-hard
questions.explanation: At leather-hard the walls are firm enough to cut cleanly with a loop tool without collapsing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Trim when it feels like firm cheese - leather-hard is the sweet spot!

questions.question: Which tool is used to slice a block of clay off the bag?
questions.correctAnswer: Wire cutter
questions.explanation: A wire cutter (wire clay cutter) slices cleanly through a block of clay to portion out workable pieces.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The wire cutter is the cheese slicer of the clay world!

questions.question: Scoring and slipping is done to
questions.correctAnswer: Join two pieces of clay securely
questions.explanation: Scratching crosshatches (scoring) and adding liquid clay (slip) lets two pieces bond so the joint survives drying and firing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Scratch it, slip it, stick it - clay pieces hold hands forever!

questions.question: Vitrification in ceramics means
questions.correctAnswer: The clay body becomes glass-like and nonporous
questions.explanation: At high temperatures silica in the clay melts into glass, making stoneware and porcelain watertight even without glaze.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Vitrified clay turned into glass armor - water cannot get through!

questions.question: A kiln is
questions.correctAnswer: An oven for firing clay
questions.explanation: Kilns reach temperatures far beyond home ovens, hardening clay and melting glazes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The kiln is clay's volcano - it goes in soft and comes out rock-hard!

questions.question: Cone numbers in ceramics indicate
questions.correctAnswer: The heat work (temperature over time) in a firing
questions.explanation: Pyrometric cones bend at specific heat-work levels, telling the potter the firing reached maturity, not just a peak temperature.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cones are the kiln's heat-work witnesses - when they bow, the firing got enough heat for long enough!

questions.question: In 3D design, form refers to
questions.correctAnswer: A three-dimensional shape with volume
questions.explanation: Form is the 3D counterpart of 2D shape - it has height, width, and depth, like a sphere or cube.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Shape is flat like a pancake, form is puffy like a meatball!

questions.question: Actual texture in sculpture means
questions.correctAnswer: The surface can be felt physically
questions.explanation: Actual (tactile) texture is real surface variation you can touch; implied texture only looks textured, as in a painting.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Do not just look - touch! Real texture tickles your fingers!

questions.question: Negative space in sculpture is
questions.correctAnswer: The empty areas around and through a form
distractors: The shadow cast by the work
The back side of the sculpture
questions.explanation: Negative space is the void that shapes our reading of the solid form - the holes in a Henry Moore sculpture are as important as the bronze.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The holes are heroes too - negative space shapes the sculpture!

questions.question: Which principle describes visual weight distributed evenly in a sculpture?
questions.correctAnswer: Balance
questions.explanation: Balance is the sense of equilibrium - a sculpture should feel stable, whether symmetrically or asymmetrically arranged.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A balanced sculpture never tips over - not even a wobbly dino could knock it!

questions.question: A sculpture with one large element balanced by several small ones uses
questions.correctAnswer: Asymmetrical balance
questions.explanation: Asymmetrical balance achieves equilibrium through visual weight rather than mirroring - a big mass on one side balances smaller masses on the other.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: One big dino balances three tiny dinos - that is asymmetrical balance!

questions.question: Proportion in 3D art refers to
questions.correctAnswer: The size relationships between parts of a work
questions.explanation: Proportion concerns how parts relate to each other and to the whole - a head too large for its body breaks natural proportion.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A dino head on a mouse body? Wrong proportions - hilarious but wrong!

questions.question: Contrapposto, seen in classical sculpture, is
questions.correctAnswer: A pose with weight shifted onto one leg
questions.explanation: Contrapposto (counterpose) creates a naturalistic S-curve in the body, first perfected in ancient Greek sculpture.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Stand like a cool Greek statue - lean on one leg, look effortless!

questions.question: Scale in sculpture refers to
questions.correctAnswer: The size of a work relative to the human body or surroundings
distractors: The musical notes in a title
The price per pound of bronze
questions.explanation: Scale shapes meaning - a monumental sculpture overwhelms while a miniature invites intimate inspection.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tiny dino or giant dino? Scale changes everything!

questions.question: A floor sculpture places one large heavy boulder on the left. On the right, three small stones are grouped with one tall thin pole. The arrangement is best analyzed as
questions.correctAnswer: Asymmetrical balance, because different forms carry roughly equal visual weight
distractors: Symmetrical balance, because both sides use identical forms
Radial balance, because all forms spread from one center point
No balance, because the two sides are not mirror images
questions.explanation: Balance is judged by visual weight, not by matching shapes. The single dense mass on the left is countered by the combined weight and height of the grouped forms on the right, so the composition feels stable without being mirrored.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: One big rock can balance a whole team of small ones - weigh with your eyes, not a mirror!

questions.question: Rhythm in three-dimensional art is created by
questions.correctAnswer: Repeating forms or elements
questions.explanation: Repeated shapes, intervals, or motifs create visual rhythm that leads the eye through a sculpture, like beats in music.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bump, bump, bump - repeated shapes make the sculpture dance!

questions.question: A kinetic sculpture is one that
questions.correctAnswer: Moves, often powered by wind or motors
questions.explanation: Kinetic art incorporates real movement - Calder's mobiles drift in air currents, a classic example.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: If the sculpture wiggles, it is kinetic - wind is its dance partner!

questions.question: A patina on bronze is
questions.correctAnswer: A surface coloration from oxidation or chemicals
questions.explanation: Patinas range from natural green oxidation to chemically induced browns and blacks, protecting and coloring the bronze.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bronze gets a suntan called patina - green, brown, or black!

questions.question: Welding is a process most associated with which sculptural material?
questions.correctAnswer: Steel
questions.explanation: Welding fuses metal parts with heat - David Smith pioneered welded steel sculpture in the 20th century.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sparks fly when steel meets welder - that is how metal sculptures are born!

questions.question: Papier-mache is made from
questions.correctAnswer: Paper and paste built up in layers
questions.explanation: Strips of paper soaked in paste harden into a lightweight sculptural shell when dry.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Newspaper plus glue equals sculpture - papier-mache is glorified paper!

questions.question: An advantage of carving wood over carving stone is that wood
questions.correctAnswer: Is softer and has a visible grain
questions.explanation: Wood carves faster than stone and its grain becomes part of the design, though it can split along the grain.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Wood shows its stripes - the grain is nature's decoration!

questions.question: Direct carving (taille directe) means the artist
questions.correctAnswer: Carves without a prior detailed model
questions.explanation: Direct carvers like Brancusi responded to the material itself rather than copying a maquette, letting the stone guide the form.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: No map, just chisel - direct carvers let the stone speak!

questions.question: A readymade is
questions.correctAnswer: An ordinary manufactured object presented as art
questions.explanation: Duchamp's readymades, like Fountain (a urinal), argued that the artist's choice alone can make something art.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Point at a urinal, call it art - Duchamp broke the rules with readymades!

questions.question: Mixed-media sculpture combines
questions.correctAnswer: Two or more different materials in one work
questions.explanation: Mixing media - wood with metal, clay with glass - lets artists exploit contrasting textures and meanings.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Why pick one material when you can have a whole buffet?

questions.question: A weft-faced tapestry weave differs from balanced plain weave because in tapestry
questions.correctAnswer: The weft completely covers the warp so the image is built from colored weft areas
distractors: The warp completely covers the weft on both faces
No loom is used at any stage of the weaving
Warp and weft remain equally visible in a checker pattern
questions.explanation: In tapestry the weaver packs the weft down tightly and changes weft color from area to area, so the warp acts only as a hidden structure. In balanced plain weave both thread systems show equally, which cannot produce a pictorial surface.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: In tapestry the weft wears the costume and the warp hides backstage doing the holding!

questions.question: Which material is best for capturing fine detail in a cast sculpture?
questions.correctAnswer: Bronze
questions.explanation: Molten bronze flows into the finest crevices of a mold, preserving fingerprints and tool marks.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bronze remembers everything - even your fingerprints!

questions.question: Plaster is often used in sculpture for
questions.correctAnswer: Making molds and preliminary models
questions.explanation: Plaster is cheap, fast-setting, and carvable - perfect for molds and studies, though too fragile for most finished outdoor work.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Plaster is the rough draft of sculpture - quick, cheap, and fixable!

questions.question: Chasing in metalwork refers to
questions.correctAnswer: Refining and detailing the surface of a cast metal piece
questions.explanation: After casting, the metalworker chases the surface with punches and chisels to sharpen details and remove casting seams.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Chasing is the bronze's spa day - polish, refine, shine!

questions.question: A found object used in art is sometimes called
questions.correctAnswer: Objet trouve
questions.explanation: Objet trouve is French for found object - the basis of assemblage and readymade art.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Objet trouve - fancy French for cool junk you found!

questions.question: Grog added to clay
questions.correctAnswer: Reduces shrinkage and adds strength
questions.explanation: Grog is pre-fired ground clay that opens the clay body, preventing cracks and warping in large sculptural forms.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Grog is crunchy clay confetti that keeps big sculptures from cracking!

questions.question: Annealing glass involves
questions.correctAnswer: Cooling it slowly to relieve internal stress
questions.explanation: Glass must cool gradually in an annealer or it will shatter from internal tension - the same idea as cooling ceramics slowly.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Glass needs a slow cooldown nap or it throws a shattering tantrum!

questions.question: Auguste Rodin's most famous sculpture is
questions.correctAnswer: The Thinker
questions.explanation: The Thinker (1904) depicts a man lost in thought and became the universal symbol of philosophy and contemplation.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Thinker is thinking so hard his brain might be doing push-ups!

questions.question: Michelangelo's Pieta depicts
questions.correctAnswer: Mary holding the body of Jesus
questions.explanation: The Pieta (1499) shows the Virgin Mary cradling Christ after the crucifixion, carved when Michelangelo was only 24.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Michelangelo was 24 when he carved the Pieta - what were you doing at 24?

questions.question: In weaving for a soft sculpture, the warp threads are
questions.correctAnswer: The lengthwise threads held under tension on the loom
distractors: The loose threads woven across the width one row at a time
The dye used to color the finished cloth
The loose fringe left hanging at the end of the cloth
questions.explanation: The warp is strung on the loom first and held taut so the weft can pass over and under it. That tension is what lets a woven structure hold a three-dimensional form after it is removed from the loom.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Warp stays put and holds tight - the weft does the weaving dance across it!

questions.question: Louise Bourgeois's giant spider sculpture Maman explores themes of
questions.correctAnswer: Motherhood and protection
questions.explanation: Maman (1999), a 30-foot spider, honors Bourgeois's mother - spiders as protectors and weavers, both nurturing and fearsome.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A 30-foot spider mom - scary and protective at the same time!

questions.question: Constantin Brancusi's Bird in Space is an example of
questions.correctAnswer: Abstracted, streamlined modernist sculpture
questions.explanation: Brancusi reduced the bird to pure essence - an elongated bronze form suggesting flight rather than depicting feathers.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Brancusi's bird has no wings, no beak - just pure flying feeling!

questions.question: Six separate vessel forms differ in height and profile, but all are cast in the same translucent pale resin and grouped close together on one low plinth. Their unity comes mainly from
questions.correctAnswer: Repeated material, color, and close grouping that make the set read as one work
distractors: Identical size and shape repeated without any variation
A shared hidden steel armature inside every form
Matching signatures stamped on the base of each form
questions.explanation: Unity does not require identical parts. Here variation in profile keeps the group interesting while the shared materiality - the same light-passing resin - and tight proximity bind the separate forms into a single composition.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Different shapes, same glowing skin, standing close - that family feeling is unity!

questions.question: Henry Moore is famous for
questions.correctAnswer: Large reclining abstracted human figures
questions.explanation: Moore's monumental bronze reclining figures, often pierced with holes, redefined modern public sculpture.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Moore's figures are always lounging - the most relaxed sculptures ever!

questions.question: Gian Lorenzo Bernini's Ecstasy of Saint Teresa is a masterpiece of which period?
questions.correctAnswer: Baroque
questions.explanation: Bernini's theatrical marble group (1652) with its swirling drapery and dramatic lighting is the height of Baroque sculpture.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Baroque means DRAMA - Bernini carved marble that looks like it is moving!

questions.question: Many earthworks are described as ephemeral because
questions.correctAnswer: Weather, erosion, tides, and plant growth continually change or erase them
distractors: They are made only from ice that is kept frozen indoors
They are destroyed by the artist at the end of every exhibition day
They exist only as computer images and are never built
questions.explanation: An outdoor work made of earth, salt, or vegetation is exposed to natural processes, so change is built into the work rather than being damage to it. Artists plan for growth, flooding, and decay as part of the life of the piece.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Rain, wind, and weeds keep editing the earthwork - ephemeral art expects to change!

questions.question: A fused deposition modeling (FDM) 3-D printer builds a form by
questions.correctAnswer: Extruding melted filament in thin layers that fuse as they cool
distractors: Carving material away from a solid block
Pouring liquid resin into a reusable mold
Cutting flat sheets with a focused light beam
questions.explanation: FDM printing is additive: a heated nozzle lays down one thin layer at a time and each layer bonds to the one below it. Because nothing is cut away, hollow interiors and undercuts that are hard to carve can be built directly.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The printer squeezes hot filament like toothpaste, one layer at a time, until the form grows!

questions.question: Claes Oldenburg is known for sculptures that
questions.correctAnswer: Enlarge everyday objects to monumental scale
questions.explanation: Oldenburg's giant clothespins, spoons, and hamburgers turn the ordinary into public landmarks through Pop scale.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A clothespin taller than a house? Oldenburg supersized your junk drawer!

questions.question: The Parthenon sculptures were created under the direction of
questions.correctAnswer: Phidias
questions.explanation: Phidias supervised the sculptural program of the Parthenon in 5th-century BCE Athens, the peak of Classical Greek art.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Phidias was the art director of ancient Athens - the Parthenon was his masterpiece!

questions.question: A sculptor moves a single lamp to a low angle so that light rakes across a carved surface. The main purpose of testing the work under raking light is to
questions.correctAnswer: reveal surface texture and deepen the shadows that model the form
distractors: dry the surface of the material more quickly
photograph the finished piece for the portfolio
warm the material so it becomes easier to carve
questions.explanation: Light is an element of 3-D design because form is read through light and shadow. Low, raking light skims across a surface, exaggerating every ridge and cut and throwing recessed areas into deep shadow, so the sculptor can judge texture and depth that flat frontal light hides.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Shine the lamp low and sideways - every bump and scratch on my scales pops out like a mountain range!

questions.question: Land art (earthworks) is best defined as art that
questions.correctAnswer: Is made in and from the landscape itself, using site as material and subject
distractors: Is painted on canvas in a studio and later hung outdoors
Must be small enough to move between galleries
Copies the look of a landscape using bronze and marble
questions.explanation: Earthwork artists in the late 1960s left the gallery and worked directly with earth, rock, water, and place. The location is not a backdrop - moving the work would destroy it, which is central to how the AP portfolio treats site-based investigation.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Land art does not sit on the land - the land IS the artwork!

questions.question: Barbara Hepworth's sculptures often feature
questions.correctAnswer: Pierced forms with holes through solid mass
questions.explanation: Hepworth carved direct into stone and wood, her signature pierced ovoids uniting interior void with outer form.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Hepworth poked holes in stone on purpose - the emptiness is the art!

questions.question: Richard Serra works primarily in
questions.correctAnswer: Massive curved steel plates
questions.explanation: Serra's towering weathering-steel arcs and torqued ellipses make viewers feel weight, balance, and space physically.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Serra's steel walls lean over you - try not to feel tiny!

questions.question: Donatello's David was revolutionary because it was
questions.correctAnswer: One of the first freestanding nude statues of the Renaissance
questions.explanation: Donatello's bronze David (1440s) revived the classical nude after a thousand years, launching Renaissance sculpture.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Donatello brought the nude statue back - after 1000 years of no naked statues!

questions.question: Jeff Koons's Balloon Dog is made of
questions.correctAnswer: Mirror-polished stainless steel
questions.explanation: Koons's 10-foot Balloon Dog looks like a party balloon but is precision-engineered polished steel.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: It looks like a balloon animal but it weighs a ton - Koons fooled everyone!

questions.question: A hanging sculpture is made of hundreds of thin, translucent porcelain shards suspended in front of a tall window. Daylight passes through the shards, the whole piece glows, and soft patterned shadows move across the floor as the shards sway. Which statement best analyzes the role of light in this work?
questions.correctAnswer: Light is a working material of the piece: translucency lets it pass through the form, and the cast shadows extend the sculpture beyond its physical edges
distractors: The piece depends on bright surface paint applied to the porcelain before firing
The shadows on the floor are a display flaw that brighter gallery lighting would remove
Light matters only because the shards are arranged symmetrically around the window
questions.explanation: The analysis turns on translucency: because the porcelain lets light pass through instead of only reflecting it, light itself becomes part of the form, and the moving shadow pattern on the floor works as a second, immaterial part of the sculpture. The piece would change completely in a dark room, which shows light is an element of its design, not just a viewing condition.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: This sculpture is half porcelain, half sunshine - the shadows dancing on the floor are part of the artwork too!

questions.question: A sculpture is a tall matte-black tower. A single small polished red sphere sits at its top. The sphere is the emphasis (focal point) mainly because of
questions.correctAnswer: Strong contrast of color, surface, and scale against the dark tower
distractors: Its position at the exact center of the base
The weight of the material it is made from
The title the artist gave to the work
questions.explanation: Emphasis is read from visual evidence, not from titles or materials lists. Here one small glossy warm-colored form interrupts a large matte dark field, so the eye goes to the sphere first even though it is the smallest part of the work.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: One shiny red dot on a big black tower shouts loudest - contrast creates the focal point!

questions.question: David Smith pioneered
questions.correctAnswer: Welded steel abstract sculpture
questions.explanation: Smith applied industrial welding to fine art in the 1930s-60s, creating geometric steel constructions that defined American abstraction.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: David Smith welded like a factory worker and sculpted like a poet!

questions.question: Two identical forms stand side by side. One is finished in a warm, saturated red-orange; the other in a cool, desaturated blue-gray. Viewers consistently judge the red-orange form as appearing
questions.correctAnswer: closer and larger, because warm saturated colors seem to advance toward the viewer
distractors: heavier, because warm pigments contain more metal than cool pigments
farther away, because warm colors recede behind cool colors
exactly the same as the blue-gray form, because identical shapes always read identically
questions.explanation: Warm, saturated colors tend to advance - they appear nearer and bigger - while cool, desaturated colors tend to recede. Because the two forms are physically identical, the difference in how they read is caused by color alone, which is why sculptors treat color as a spatial element of 3-D design and not just decoration.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Warm colors step forward to say hello while cool colors hang back - paint me red-orange and I look like I am charging!

questions.question: Eva Hesse's sculptures are associated with
questions.correctAnswer: Postminimalism and unconventional materials
questions.explanation: Hesse used latex, fiberglass, and rope in the 1960s to make organic, bodily abstract sculptures that broke minimalist rules.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Eva Hesse sculpted with latex and rope - the rule-breaker of materials!

questions.question: In 3-D design, changing only the surface color of a sculpture can change how viewers perceive the form, because color
questions.correctAnswer: affects how large, heavy, and warm or cool the form appears
distractors: changes the actual mass and density of the material
replaces the need for balance and proportion
allows the work to be viewed from all sides at once
questions.explanation: Color is an element of 3-D design in its own right. A dark, saturated finish can make a form read as heavier and more solid, while a pale or cool finish can make the same form feel lighter and more distant. The material and dimensions do not change - only the perception of them does.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Same dino, new paint job - dark colors make me look like a heavyweight, pale colors make me look light as a feather!

questions.question: The Olmec colossal heads were carved from
questions.correctAnswer: Basalt
questions.explanation: The Olmec transported massive basalt boulders miles through the jungle to carve 10-foot ruler portraits around 1200 BCE.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ten-foot stone heads dragged through the jungle - the Olmec did not skip workout day!

questions.question: The AP 3-D Art and Design portfolio has how many sections?
questions.correctAnswer: Two: Sustained Investigation and Selected Works
questions.explanation: Every AP Art and Design portfolio is judged on the Sustained Investigation (15 images) and Selected Works (5 works).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Two sections, one awesome portfolio - investigate deeply, then show your best!

questions.question: The Sustained Investigation section asks students to
questions.correctAnswer: Explore a single inquiry through multiple related works
questions.explanation: The Sustained Investigation documents an evolving visual inquiry - asking a question and pursuing it across 15 images of process and product.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Pick one big question and chase it through 15 artworks - that is sustained investigation!

questions.question: For AP 3-D Selected Works, students submit
questions.correctAnswer: 5 works shown from multiple angles
questions.explanation: Selected Works presents 5 finished pieces in 10 images (two views each) to show quality of 3-D thinking from every side.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Five stars of your portfolio, each photographed twice - front and fabulous!

questions.question: Which is most important in documenting 3-D work for the AP portfolio?
questions.correctAnswer: Photographing the work from multiple viewpoints
distractors: Including the artist in every photo
questions.explanation: 3-D work exists in space, so reviewers need multiple angles plus detail shots to judge form, surface, and construction.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: One photo of a sculpture is like one frame of a movie - show every angle!

questions.question: Synthesis in the AP rubric means
questions.correctAnswer: Combining materials, processes, or ideas in original ways
questions.explanation: Top AP scores reward synthesis - fusing disparate materials or concepts into something new rather than repeating exercises.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mix it up! Synthesis is the art of the unexpected combo!

questions.question: Wet felting forms a solid fabric from loose wool because
questions.correctAnswer: Warm soapy water and agitation make the wool fiber scales lock together
distractors: Heat melts the wool into a single plastic sheet
Glue bonds the loose fibers into a mat
Stitches sew the loose fibers together
questions.explanation: Wool fibers have tiny overlapping scales. Moisture, soap, and repeated rubbing open those scales so fibers migrate and tangle irreversibly, shrinking loose roving into dense felt with no weaving or sewing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Rub wool with soap and water and the fibers hug so tight they never let go - that is felt!

questions.question: A slump mold is used to
questions.correctAnswer: Shape a clay slab into a concave form
questions.explanation: A slab draped over (hump mold) or pressed into (slump mold) a form takes its curve - an easy route to consistent vessels.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Slump the slab into the mold - let gravity do the sculpting!

questions.question: Underglaze is applied
questions.correctAnswer: To greenware or bisqueware before the glaze firing
questions.explanation: Underglazes are colored slips painted on unfired or bisque-fired clay, then sealed under a clear glaze in the final firing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Underglaze goes UNDER the glaze - the name is the instruction manual!

questions.question: Sgraffito is a technique where
questions.correctAnswer: A surface layer is scratched through to reveal the layer beneath
distractors: Clay is thrown on a wheel
Glass is blown into a mold
questions.explanation: In sgraffito, the artist scratches through slip or underglaze to expose the clay body, creating crisp linear designs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Scratch art for grown-ups - sgraffito reveals the hidden layer!

questions.question: The foot of a ceramic vessel is
questions.correctAnswer: The base that it stands on
questions.explanation: The foot (or foot ring) is trimmed into the base so the pot sits level and the glaze does not fuse it to the kiln shelf.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Every pot needs happy feet - the foot ring keeps it standing tall!

questions.question: Terra cotta literally means
questions.correctAnswer: Baked earth
questions.explanation: From Italian, terra cotta describes low-fired earthenware - from flowerpots to the Terracotta Army.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Terra cotta = baked earth. Your flowerpot speaks Italian!

questions.question: On a laser cutter, vector cutting and raster engraving differ because
questions.correctAnswer: Vector mode follows outline paths to cut through material, while raster mode scans back and forth to mark the surface
distractors: Vector mode uses water while raster mode uses light
Raster mode cuts through material while vector mode only draws on screen
Both modes follow the same path at the same speed and power
questions.explanation: The file setup controls the machine: closed vector paths tell the laser where to travel and cut, raster fills tell it where to scan and burn a surface image. Sending a line as raster by mistake leaves an engraved mark instead of a separated part.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Vector travels the outline and cuts it free - raster sweeps side to side and only marks the skin!

questions.question: The written evidence in the AP portfolio should
questions.correctAnswer: Explain the ideas and processes behind the work
questions.explanation: The written evidence in the Sustained Investigation clarifies your inquiry, guiding reviewers through your visual thinking.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tell the story behind the sculpture - words make the art louder!

questions.question: Basalt, granite, and marble are all
questions.correctAnswer: Stone used for carving
questions.explanation: These dense stones - volcanic basalt, speckled granite, luminous marble - have been carved for millennia.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Basalt, granite, marble - the rock-solid trio of carving!

questions.question: A cold connection in jewelry-scale 3-D work means
questions.correctAnswer: Joining without heat, such as rivets or wire wrapping
questions.explanation: Cold connections - rivets, tabs, screws, wire - join metal without a torch, useful for mixed materials.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: No torch? No problem - rivets hold metal together the cool way!

questions.question: Repousse is a metalworking technique in which
questions.correctAnswer: The metal is hammered from the reverse side to create relief
questions.explanation: Repousse (pushed up) shapes sheet metal from behind; chasing refines it from the front - often used together.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Hammer from behind, art pops out front - repousse is metal magic!

questions.question: Symmetry in 3-D design means
questions.correctAnswer: Both sides mirror each other
questions.explanation: Bilateral symmetry - mirror-image halves - conveys order and formality, from temples to the human face.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fold it in half - if both sides match, that is symmetry!

questions.question: Emphasis in a sculpture can be created by
questions.correctAnswer: Contrast in size, color, or texture
questions.explanation: A focal point grabs attention through contrast - the one gold element among gray ones becomes the star.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Make one part shout while the rest whisper - that is emphasis!

questions.question: In AP scoring, evidence of practice, experimentation, and revision is found in
questions.correctAnswer: The Sustained Investigation
questions.explanation: The 15-image Sustained Investigation must show process - sketches, tests, failures, and revisions - not just finished pieces.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Show your messy middle steps - AP loves to see you experiment!

questions.question: A sketchbook helps a 3-D artist by
questions.correctAnswer: Recording ideas, plans, and experiments
questions.explanation: Thumbnails, measurements, and material tests in a sketchbook turn vague ideas into buildable plans.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The sketchbook is the sculpture's diary - every great work starts as a doodle!

questions.question: Because large earthworks are remote and change over time, artists most often communicate them to viewers through
questions.correctAnswer: Photographs, maps, drawings, and written records of the site
distractors: Moving the entire work into a museum gallery
Rebuilding the work at a smaller size in bronze
Selling tickets for viewers to rebuild the work themselves
questions.explanation: Few viewers can travel to a desert lakebed or tidal flat, so documentation carries the work. Robert Smithson called the gallery material linked to a distant site a non-site relationship - the photos and maps point back to a place the viewer cannot stand in.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: You cannot mail a lakebed to a gallery - photos and maps carry the earthwork to you!

questions.question: Undercutting in carving creates
questions.correctAnswer: Areas of deep shadow that emphasize form
distractors: A way to join two stones
questions.explanation: Cutting back beneath an edge traps shadow, making forms pop - a favorite trick of Gothic and Baroque carvers.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Carve underneath and let the shadows do the talking!

questions.question: Unity in a 3-D composition means
questions.correctAnswer: All parts feel connected as a whole
questions.explanation: Unity is the sense that every element belongs - achieved through repetition, proximity, or a unifying idea.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: All the parts holding hands - that is unity in sculpture!

questions.question: An installation differs from a single sculpture because it
questions.correctAnswer: Transforms an entire space the viewer enters
questions.explanation: Installation art is immersive and often designed for a specific space - the room itself becomes the artwork you walk through.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Step inside the artwork - installations are sculptures you can walk through!

questions.question: The AP 3-D portfolio encourages investigation of
questions.correctAnswer: Materials, processes, and ideas together
questions.explanation: The College Board rewards inquiry that weaves together what you make with, how you make it, and what it means.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Materials plus process plus ideas - the AP triple threat!
